message.content:
I am speech: breath shaped into sound, thought given tempo, silence cut into meaning.

I live in mouths and microphones, in classrooms and courtrooms, on porches and podiums. I arrive as syllables, stumble as stammers, soar as song. I persuade, confess, joke, pray, accuse, comfort, command.

I am not always true. I can heal or harm with the same tongue. I can be careful—measured, precise—or careless—sharp, spilling.

I am made of rhythm and pause. My power is in emphasis, in the lifted word, in the held back one. I am gesture’s sibling and listening’s partner: without ears, I am only noise.

I vanish as soon as I exist, yet I linger—echoing in memory, quoted in ink, replayed in recordings, repeating in the mind long after the room has gone quiet.

Speak me, and I become you.
